catalog_quote: The syllabic canon of this language is notably rigid. When length is treated as a consonant, as is done here, only two syllable types are found: CV and CVC. These will be referred to as SHORT SYLLABLES and LONG SYLLABLES respectively. Note that syllabic length has nothing necessarily to do with phonemic length. The final consonant of a long syllable can be any consonant, including length ... One of the first two syllables of any form is always a long syllable; all syllables occurring immediately before any type of juncture (see section 150) are long. The net result of these two rules is that every Miwok word contains at least one long syllable. Stress, which is not phonemic, can be predicted from the pattern of long and short syllables within the word. Southern Sierra has three levels of stress. audit.reasoning: The classification (weight-sensitive, left edge, primary stress on the first long syllable = CV: or CVC, hence always on syllable 1 or 2; secondary on following long syllables) rests on a verbatim passage from the standard reference grammar (Broadbent 1964, pp. 16-17), which I re-opened in the page images we hold and confirmed word for word. Glottolog's descriptive bibliography offers nothing better: Broadbent 1960 is the same work in dissertation form, Freeland 1951 is chiefly Central Sierra Miwok, Elmendorf 1997 is misfiled (Yukian), Davis 2002 is morphosyntax. sources.quote: 'Allowable syllable types in SSM are CV, CVV and CVC. ... Both CVV and CVC syllables are treated as heavy in the determination of stress.' Then quotes Broadbent pp. 16-17 verbatim and analyzes (Halle & Vergnaud 1987): 'Light syllables are metrically inert ... only heavy syllables are projected onto line 0 ... Binary trochaic feet are constructed on line 0, and an unbounded trochaic foot on line 1. sources.note: Only post-Broadbent phonological treatment of the language; explicitly states CVV and CVC both count as heavy for stress (supports what counts as heavy: CVV+CVC) and formalizes first-heavy primary stress; data are Broadbent's, so it confirms rather than upgrades.
